messages.author: 07b82b69b78faed3
messages.subject: Fit Measures in DWLS
parts:
Thanks for all of the great work. This package is phenomenal.

I have recently been reading that CFi and perhaps some other fit measures are not appropriate in DWLS, or at least the traditional cutoff values reported by Hu & Bentler are not appropriate for models estimated by DWLS. For a nice review of what has been written I will refer people to methods section of a free article published in PLOS One: http://www.plosone.org/article/info%3Adoi%2F10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0061191

The above article takes the approach of using RMSEA and RMSR to assess model fit (both of which lavaan supplies), applying Hu and Bentler Criteria. However, it seems that other fit measures can also be used. For example, SAS modifies the GFI for WLS and DWLS ( http://www.math.wpi.edu/saspdf/stat/chap19.pdf page 539).

Does lavaan use a special estimation procedures for GFI in cases of DWLS, or does it simply apply the same GFI estimation procedure to all estimators?

Also, is there a preferred index of model fit with DWLS in lavaan?


-Paul

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Fit Measures in DWLS
parts:
On 05/01/2013 04:34 PM, Paul Gerrard wrote:

> The above article takes the approach of using RMSEA and RMSR to assess
> model fit (both of which lavaan supplies), applying Hu and Bentler
> Criteria. However, it seems that other fit measures can also be used.
> For example, SAS modifies the GFI for WLS and DWLS
> ( http://www.math.wpi.edu/saspdf/stat/chap19.pdf page 539).

The SAS manual shows two different equations, but the upper one can be
rewritten as the lower one (given an appropriate choice for W). So there
is really only one definition of GFI, for all estimators.

> Does lavaan use a special estimation procedures for GFI in cases of
> DWLS, or does it simply apply the same GFI estimation procedure to all
> estimators?

lavaan uses one approach for all estimators; from the source code in
fit.Measures.R (for single group 'g'):

wls.diff <- wls.obs - wls.est
t1 <- crossprod(wls.diff, wls.v) %*% wls.diff
t2 <- crossprod(wls.obs, wls.v) %*% wls.obs
gfi.group[g] <- 1 - t1/t2

where wls.v is computed differently depending on the estimator

wls.v <- lavaan:::getWLS.V(fit)[[g]]

and g is the group number.

Yves.
